items.t: Snowys Outdoors finds malicious code on its retail website

rec.title: Snowys Outdoors finds malicious code on its retail website
rec.summary: Snowys said malicious code on its website targeted information customers entered between October 5 and November 16. Customer contact details and passwords entered on the site may have been captured, but Snowys could not confirm that an attacker received them and reported no indication that payment cards were involved.
affected: Snowys customers who entered details at checkout, signed in, or registered during the affected period.
payloads: The code targeted information entered into checkout and account forms. Snowys found no evidence that the customer database was copied.
guidance: Set a new Snowys password when prompted, and change the same or similar passwords on other services.
Use a unique password for every service and go directly to the retailer’s site to verify unexpected account messages.

items.t: LaLiga confirms theft of personal data from a fan-services platform

rec.title: LaLiga confirms theft of personal data from a fan-services platform
rec.summary: LaLiga said someone accessed one fan-services platform between November 14 and 16 and took personal data from users of LaLiga digital services and some clubs. LaLiga contained the attack on November 16 and notified affected clubs, Spain’s data protection authority and national police. It did not publish a count or specify the types of data taken.

sources.label: Europa Press reporting on LaLiga’s notice

affected: People registered with LaLiga digital services and services of some clubs; the clubs and number of people were not disclosed.
payloads: LaLiga confirmed personal data was taken from a single fan-services platform. It reported no impact on other systems or on matches.
guidance: Watch for messages impersonating LaLiga or a club, and verify any instructions through the official fan-services account.
Review access and export logs, check for unusual account activity, and notify affected users with precise scope as it is established.

guidance: Change the website password anywhere it was reused. Treat unsolicited messages using your contact information with caution.
Preserve and review access logs, invalidate affected sessions and verify password storage protections before restoring affected services.

Review mint privileges and recent changes, suspend compromised permissions, and alert on abnormal mint volumes and discrepancies between minted supply and reserves.

items.t: KEPCO confirms breach of customer service and procurement systems

rec.title: KEPCO confirms breach of customer service and procurement systems
rec.summary: Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) confirmed exposure for 650,487 users of its billing platform. It reported a separate procurement-system breach and treated all 869,761 procurement users as potentially affected because it could not establish the precise scope. The combined count does not establish how many distinct people had data exposed.

sources.label: Aju Press on confirmed exposure and notification scope
Chosun Ilbo on the two systems and possible overlap
SBS quoting KEPCO on the procurement notification scope

updates.text: Daily Secu reported a November 19 allegation involving KEPCO user and bidding data. The report did not establish the origin of the claimed data or whether it is connected to the confirmed breach.
KEPCO said it detected the leak on November 20, blocked external access and suspended affected services while investigating.

SBS reported that procurement data was exposed. It separately quoted KEPCO saying it treated all procurement users as potentially affected because it could not establish individual exposure; overlap with the billing cohort remains unresolved.
Daily Secu reported KEPCO’s confirmation but said it had not established whether the earlier forum claim and the confirmed breach covered the same data.
South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission launched an investigation and planned on-site checks. It did not announce a revised count of affected people.

affected: KEPCO ON electricity customers and users of KEPCO’s electronic procurement system. The precise number of procurement users whose data was exposed was not established.
payloads: The billing platform exposure included identity, contact, billing and payment data. Aju Press reported that certain identity numbers and card numbers were stored encrypted. The scope within procurement remains under investigation.
guidance: Look up notices through the official utility website rather than following unsolicited links about bills or compensation.
Monitor bank and card activity and contact your provider through a verified number about unfamiliar transactions.
Preserve access and export logs, verify the scope of data access in each service, and reconcile notified users before reporting a distinct-person total.

rec.title: Cleverbridge confirms theft of payment-card data

affected: Cleverbridge
Affected cardholders who purchased through Cleverbridge; the company did not identify specific merchants.
payloads: Stored payment-card data was copied; Cleverbridge did not disclose the access method. The company said this was not ransomware and its systems were not encrypted.
guidance: Check statements and contact the card issuer about unknown transactions or a replacement card.
Verify that notices are authentic through the official incident FAQ; never share card details in response to unsolicited messages.
Review payment-data retention and payment-provider incident response with vendors.

rec.summary: The Herald Business reported that the impact of Streami’s previously announced leak rose from 9 to 2,009 people. The original disclosure was in October; the exact day was not verified. The report does not establish a link to the separate November trading freeze.

sources.label: The Herald Business coverage of the revised count
Digital Today coverage of the regulator’s response

updates.text: The Herald Business reported a revised total of 2,009 affected individuals.

items.t: SeaHorses Mikawa warns former shop customers after One’s Closet breach

rec.title: SeaHorses Mikawa warns former shop customers after One’s Closet breach
rec.summary: SeaHorses Mikawa said its former online-shop provider One’s Closet reported unauthorized access and theft of data. Up to 835 former shop customers may be affected. The team did not confirm that all potentially affected customers’ data was taken.
affected: Former SeaHorses Mikawa online shop customers
One’s Closet storefront platform
payloads: The shop notice did not describe malware.
guidance: Be alert for unsolicited messages referring to previous orders; verify through the team’s official contact channels.

items.t: LEGOLAND Japan warns of possible exposure at annual-pass platform

rec.title: LEGOLAND Japan warns of possible exposure at annual-pass platform
rec.summary: LEGOLAND Japan said annual-pass platform operator accesso reported unauthorized access. About 150,000 buyers may be affected, including former passholders. Data potentially involved contact and demographic details and pass barcode numbers. The notice did not identify payment-card or bank-account exposure.
affected: Annual-pass customer data held by accesso
payloads: No malicious payload was disclosed.
guidance: Verify messages through LEGOLAND Japan’s official channels; do not disclose payment credentials in response to unsolicited contact.

items.t: E Ink investigates possible attack on information systems

rec.title: E Ink investigates possible attack on information systems
rec.summary: E Ink Holdings said it suspected its information systems had been targeted and retained outside experts. Its preliminary assessment found no material operational impact. The company did not confirm unauthorized access or data theft.

items.t: Gleneagle Killarney confirms guest reservation data exposure at booking provider

rec.title: Gleneagle Killarney confirms guest reservation data exposure at booking provider
rec.summary: The Gleneagle Hotel in Killarney said unauthorized access to its booking-system provider exposed guest reservation information. Its notice also covered Hotel67 and Gleneagle River Apartments, which operate on the same property. The hotel said payment and banking information were not involved.

sources.label: The Echo, quoting the Gleneagle statement

affected: Gleneagle Hotel, Hotel67 and Gleneagle River Apartments in Killarney, Ireland.
payloads: Guest names, email addresses, booking references and stay dates. The hotel excluded payment details, banking information and passwords.
guidance: Verify unexpected requests for payment or personal information through the hotel’s official contact details.

items.t: MUFG Bank reports exposure of demographic data through KARTE

rec.title: MUFG Bank reports exposure of demographic data through KARTE
rec.summary: MUFG Bank reported exposure of about 6.5 million records through PLAID’s KARTE service. It said the affected information did not allow outsiders to identify or contact customers.

items.t: Pai Chai University reports exposure from learning and academic systems

rec.title: Pai Chai University reports exposure from learning and academic systems
rec.summary: Pai Chai University said unauthorized access exposed some personal information from its learning management and connected academic systems. It isolated the affected systems, reset portal passwords and required multifactor authentication.

sources.label: ZDNET Korea, reporting the university notice

items.t: Iwamizawa investigates possible property-tax data exposure at subcontractor

rec.title: Iwamizawa investigates possible property-tax data exposure at subcontractor
rec.summary: Iwamizawa said a subcontractor found malware on equipment holding city property-tax information. The city has not verified disclosure or misuse, or established a link to the separate NIKKE incident.

items.t: Kaspersky reports AuditTeam ransomware activity across seven countries and territories

rec.title: Kaspersky reports AuditTeam ransomware activity across seven countries and territories
rec.summary: Kaspersky linked AuditTeam to compromises at dozens of organizations between January and October 2026. Its researchers identified the OpsAgent malware framework in the observed attacks.

items.t: Police report resolution after unauthorized access to a patient's hospital record
items.x: insider leak · healthcare · GB · hospital staff · unauthorized staff access to a patient record

rec.title: Police report resolution after unauthorized access to a patient's hospital record
rec.summary: Cambridge University Hospitals confirmed it dismissed three employees for improperly accessing one patient's medical record. Police later said two people received community resolutions that included writing apology letters; the follow-up did not disclose new access.
rec.vector: unauthorized staff access to a patient record

updates.text: BBC reported that two community resolutions included apology letters, following earlier improper access to a patient record.

items.t: Rokkatei reports possible exposure of card data after online-store breach
items.x: data breach · retail · JP · altered online checkout

rec.title: Rokkatei reports possible exposure of card data after online-store breach
rec.summary: Rokkatei found unauthorized changes to its online shop. It said payment and contact information entered while the shop was affected may have been captured, and confirmed one case of fraudulent card use. A full affected count is not established.

updates.text: Rokkatei said customer personal information may also have been exposed, in addition to previously disclosed potential payment-card exposure. It did not give a new deduplicated count.
Yomiuri reported that Rokkatei confirmed one case of card misuse after a customer reported it. Other personal information may also have been exposed.

items.t: DHC reports approximately 19.11 million records exposed through KARTE
items.x: third-party breach · retail · JP · compromised third-party marketing platform

rec.title: DHC reports approximately 19.11 million records exposed through KARTE
rec.summary: DHC said customer information was exposed in the PLAID KARTE breach. The roughly 19.11 million figure counts records, not verified unique people; DHC said card data and its online shop passwords were not included.

items.t: Ransomware halts Osaki Electric smart-meter production
items.x: ransomware · manufacturing · JP · Qilin (claimed) · suspected compromise of VPN authentication, per Osaki Electric

rec.title: Ransomware halts Osaki Electric smart-meter production
rec.summary: Osaki Electric said a ransomware attack, believed to have entered via a VPN device, forced it to halt production and shipment of smart meters; resumption timing is undecided. Technical information may have been posted online, and the Qilin group claimed the attack.
rec.vector: suspected compromise of VPN authentication, per Osaki Electric

updates.text: Osaki dated the likely intrusion to November 15, confirmed some servers were encrypted on November 17, and said backups were intact. The size of the possible data exposure and the timetable to resume production remained unknown.

items.t: Norwegian utility Skagerak Energi hit by attempted cyberattack
items.x: vulnerability exploitation · energy · NO · exploited Microsoft Azure API Management vulnerability

rec.title: Norwegian utility Skagerak Energi hit by attempted cyberattack
rec.summary: Norwegian power company Skagerak Energi reported an attempted cyberattack on 18 November and later said operations were back to normal. Norway's NSM linked it to the same Azure API Management vulnerability used against Equinor.
rec.vector: exploited Microsoft Azure API Management vulnerability

items.t: Cyberattacks on Basel-Landschaft administration; 97,000 cross-border worker records stolen

rec.title: Cyberattacks on Basel-Landschaft administration; 97,000 cross-border worker records stolen
rec.summary: The Swiss canton of Basel-Landschaft said its administration had been under cyberattack since 15 November, affecting about 20 applications. About 97,000 records relating to cross-border worker permits were stolen.

items.t: Cyberattack on ISP Wittenberg-net cuts internet and phone for thousands of households

rec.title: Cyberattack on ISP Wittenberg-net cuts internet and phone for thousands of households
rec.summary: Saxony-Anhalt internet provider Wittenberg-net was hit by a hacker attack that disrupted landline and internet service for more than 8,000 households.

items.t: EV-charging app Chargemap says user data stolen in 8 November attack

rec.title: EV-charging app Chargemap says user data stolen in 8 November attack
rec.summary: French EV-charging app Chargemap said an attack on 8 November exposed users' names, email addresses, phone numbers and password hashes. The service has about 3.5 million users; the number affected was not specified.

items.t: TfL says data of 265,000 Oyster photocard holders exposed

rec.title: TfL says data of 265,000 Oyster photocard holders exposed
rec.summary: Transport for London said it detected suspicious activity on 16 November affecting its Oyster photocard system, exposing data of about 265,000 people.

items.t: The Gentlemen ransomware group claims NVIDIA data; NVIDIA probes partner incident
items.x: extortion claim · technology · US · The Gentlemen

rec.title: The Gentlemen ransomware group claims NVIDIA data; NVIDIA probes partner incident
rec.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group listed NVIDIA on its leak site on 18 November with a 28 November deadline, without proof. NVIDIA said it found no indication its own systems were affected and is investigating an incident that may involve a third party.

items.t: N-able says breach of Mail Assure/SpamExperts servers caused major outage

rec.title: N-able says breach of Mail Assure/SpamExperts servers caused major outage
rec.summary: N-able reported unauthorized access to one server supporting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud. Management services were temporarily disabled; mail flow and spam filtering continued.

updates.text: N-able said it fixed CVE-2026-134624 and restored dashboard and API access. Mail flow and filtering continued throughout, and it found no evidence of exploitation beyond one hosted server.

affected: N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud; the company identified one compromised hosted server.
payloads: Unauthorized server access was identified. N-able patched CVE-2026-134624 and is investigating the root cause with outside responders.
guidance: Use the vendor status update to verify access restoration. Self-managed deployments should check the vendor’s update guidance, review access logs, and alert on unexpected server-to-server connections.

items.t: Fayetteville Public Library says patron account information accessed

rec.title: Fayetteville Public Library says patron account information accessed
rec.summary: Fayetteville Public Library in Arkansas said patron account information in its catalogue system was accessed in a security incident on 16 November.

items.t: KPMG Canada says third party accessed client tax documents

rec.title: KPMG Canada says third party accessed client tax documents
rec.summary: KPMG Canada said on 18 November that an unauthorised third party accessed client tax documents.

items.t: Banco do Brasil alerts customers after misuse of valid credential exposes account data
items.x: data breach · finance · BR · misuse of a valid credential

rec.title: Banco do Brasil alerts customers after misuse of valid credential exposes account data
rec.summary: Banco do Brasil said misuse of a valid credential exposed customers' names, CPF numbers, emails and branch and account numbers, while denying its systems were hacked. Criminals claimed to hold data of 22.7 million customers; the bank has not confirmed that figure.

items.t: Ethiopian Airlines investigates breach of ShebaMiles loyalty accounts

rec.title: Ethiopian Airlines investigates breach of ShebaMiles loyalty accounts
rec.summary: Ethiopian Airlines notified ShebaMiles frequent-flyer members on 18 November of unauthorised access to customer information, and its CEO confirmed an investigation.

updates.text: New reporting noted 5.38 million program accounts, not the number compromised. The airline has not published the number affected.

items.t: Swedish beauty retailer Lyko says up to 50,000 customers' personal data stolen

rec.title: Swedish beauty retailer Lyko says up to 50,000 customers' personal data stolen
rec.summary: Lyko detected unauthorized access in an isolated system on November 12 and says it stopped the intrusion within an hour. Follow-up reporting put the affected count at about 60,000 customers, including 36,000 in Sweden.

updates.text: Lyko’s revised count is about 60,000 affected customers, including around 36,000 in Sweden.

items.t: Bulgaria disrupts five-year cyber-espionage operation that stole 62 million pages of government documents

rec.title: Bulgaria disrupts five-year cyber-espionage operation that stole 62 million pages of government documents
rec.summary: Bulgaria's government said on 18 November it had disrupted the longest-running known cyber-espionage operation against its state administration, in which hacker groups had access for about five years. More than 130 GB of data, equivalent to 62 million pages of documents, was downloaded; access has been blocked, prosecutors were notified, and officials said there is no evidence so far that citizens' personal data was compromised.

sources.label: Security Affairs on the previously disclosed espionage case

items.t: Hackers publish some patient data from Trieste private hospital Policlinico Triestino

rec.title: Hackers publish some patient data from Trieste private hospital Policlinico Triestino
rec.summary: Trieste private hospital Policlinico Triestino (Salus) was hit by a cyberattack and some personal and health-related patient data was published on the dark web. The hospital said all clinical reports remained secure.

items.t: Hack of savings-bank staff training site exposes data of 10,244 employees
items.x: third-party breach · finance · KR · unauthorised access to training-management site

rec.title: Hack of savings-bank staff training site exposes data of 10,244 employees
rec.summary: A training-management site for South Korean savings-bank employees, operated by KG Eduone, was accessed without authorisation between 01:49 and 04:57 on 15 November. Personal data of 10,244 employees, including affiliations, positions, names and phone numbers, leaked; the Korea Federation of Savings Banks warned of impersonation scams.

items.t: Hack of Jeonju University online course system leaks about 180,000 records

rec.title: Hack of Jeonju University online course system leaks about 180,000 records
rec.summary: Jeonju University said its online liberal-arts course system was hacked, leaking about 180,000 records of students and staff, including about 25,000 resident registration numbers. The service was suspended and the incident reported to authorities.

items.o: Yeungnam, Kyungil, Daegu Haany, Pusan National and Dongeui universities
items.t: Wave of hacks at South Korean universities in Daegu-Gyeongbuk and Busan leaks personal data

rec.org: Yeungnam, Kyungil, Daegu Haany, Pusan National and Dongeui universities
rec.title: Wave of hacks at South Korean universities in Daegu-Gyeongbuk and Busan leaks personal data
rec.summary: Several South Korean universities reported hacks in mid-November: Kyungil University (about 3,000 records via its e-document system), Daegu Haany University (about 1,200 records via its research ERP), and Yeungnam University (library e-book and careers sites, 16 November). Pusan National University's research-administration system and Dongeui University were hacked on 14 November, leaking roughly 500 records each.

items.t: Mobile local-currency platform Chak leaks data of 566 Chungnam users

rec.title: Mobile local-currency platform Chak leaks data of 566 Chungnam users
rec.summary: South Chungcheong Province said personal data of 566 users in 12 cities and counties leaked from the mobile local-currency platform Chak, including names and dates of birth. The province warned residents about secondary damage.

items.t: Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package compromised to steal cloud and CI credentials
items.x: supply chain · technology · multi · malicious package versions published to PyPI

rec.title: Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package compromised to steal cloud and CI credentials
rec.summary: Two unauthorized Microsoft Agent Framework package versions exposed developer credentials and were removed from PyPI. Wiz reported three confirmed cases of data theft and said the attacker appears to have used compromised credentials for Microsoft’s release pipeline. How the pipeline credentials were obtained remains unknown.
rec.vector: malicious package versions published to PyPI

updates.text: Wiz identified a suspected compromise of Microsoft release-pipeline credentials and three confirmed cases of data exfiltration.

rec.summary: Valley Family Health Care, Inc. issued a notice on 18 November of a data security incident that may have exposed patients' Social Security numbers and medical information.

items.x: third-party breach · retail · CA · compromised e-commerce platform

rec.title: Charlottetown hobby shop Exor Games warns customers of data leak via e-commerce platform
rec.summary: Exor Games in Charlottetown, P.E.I., emailed customers that scammers appear to have obtained their purchase history and personal information through its e-commerce platform more than a year ago.

items.t: K3 Capital's sBOLD vault exploited for about $3.43 million

rec.title: K3 Capital's sBOLD vault exploited for about $3.43 million
rec.summary: K3 Capital's sBOLD savings vault on Ethereum was exploited for about $3.43 million on 18 November, Blockaid said, and K3 paused the contracts. Ethereum block builders captured much of the value through MEV.

updates.text: K3’s post-mortem reported about 3.43 million BOLD drained from the sBOLD vault and described efforts to recover funds; it said Liquity V2 was unaffected.

items.t: Gonka's Ethereum bridge exploited for about $1.05 million, WGNK minted
items.x: crypto exploit · crypto · multi · bridge exploit (unauthorised WGNK minting)

rec.title: Gonka's Ethereum bridge exploited for about $1.05 million, WGNK minted
rec.summary: Gonka's Ethereum bridge was exploited on 18 November: the attacker withdrew about 884,000 in stablecoins and minted about 22 million WGNK, with losses estimated at $1.05 million. Gonka said its network was unaffected and told users not to trade WGNK or use the bridge.

updates.text: Gonka said all funds had been returned.

items.t: Reental's Polygon lending contracts drained after admin upgrade
items.x: crypto exploit · crypto · ES · admin-controlled contract upgrade

rec.title: Reental's Polygon lending contracts drained after admin upgrade
rec.summary: Spanish real-estate tokenisation platform Reental's RNT Lend contracts on Polygon were drained on 18 November after an attacker gained access through an admin-controlled contract upgrade. Reported losses were about $454,000; Bitquery found about $955,000 left the app, with MEV bots taking roughly half.

rec.org: Credential theft campaign reported by Hunt.io

rec.summary: Hunt.io found stolen bank, government and password-manager credentials in data from a malware operation targeting users' own Windows computers. rec.summary: LUKSO says an incident in its email-based recovery service affected about 300 Universal Profiles and resulted in the theft of about 1.4 million LYX. LUKSO said it stopped the attack and that the blockchain and core protocol were not affected.

rec.title: Researcher reports CreditNirvana exposure affecting 6.6 million accounts

rec.title: Open Group confirms unauthorized access to BizRobo!mini authentication environment

items.t: HUMAN disrupts BADBOX 3.0 ad fraud and residential proxy operation

rec.title: HUMAN disrupts BADBOX 3.0 ad fraud and residential proxy operation
rec.summary: HUMAN disrupted an ad-fraud botnet operating on infected consumer streaming boxes and other low-cost devices. It measured about 40 billion ad bid requests per day at peak, not 40 billion devices or people. The operation also used victims’ internet connections without consent.
affected: Consumers with infected streaming devices; HUMAN did not disclose a unique victim count.
payloads: Infected devices generated hidden advertising traffic and shared home internet connections without owners’ knowledge.
guidance: Use certified Android TV devices and keep Google Play Protect active. Isolate devices suspected of infection and replace them if trusted supported firmware is unavailable.

items.t: Bitdefender finds malicious GitHub projects targeting AI coding assistants

rec.title: Bitdefender finds malicious GitHub projects targeting AI coding assistants
rec.summary: Bitdefender found 22 malicious GitHub links that targeted developers using AI coding assistants. The content was designed to steal credentials and spread, but the report did not establish successful theft or a victim count. The targeted assistants were not shown to have been compromised as products.
affected: Developers who ran untrusted GitHub projects with AI coding assistants
payloads: Malicious repository content sought execution in developers’ workspaces to steal credentials and spread.
guidance: Inspect unfamiliar repository instructions and automation before trusting a workspace.
Isolate agent sessions from secrets and require approval for shell and network access.
If untrusted code ran, review source-control and cloud activity and revoke potentially exposed credentials.

items.t: Mandiant links two U.S. cloud intrusions to COLD RELIC
items.x: state intrusion · not disclosed · US · COLD RELIC (Mandiant attribution) · Credential compromise and impersonation, as assessed by investigators.

rec.title: Mandiant links two U.S. cloud intrusions to COLD RELIC
rec.summary: Mandiant linked two investigated intrusions at unnamed U.S. organizations, one in late 2025 and the other in 2026, to the group it tracks as COLD RELIC. The investigators assess that information from the first intrusion helped the actor impersonate an employee and gain access at the second organization.
rec.vector: Credential compromise and impersonation, as assessed by investigators.

sources.label: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant investigation

affected: Two unnamed U.S. organizations investigated by Mandiant.
payloads: The actor accessed cloud files and is assessed to have reused information from the first organization to impersonate an employee at the second.
guidance: Require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication for privileged users and verify sensitive requests through a second, known channel.
During containment, revoke sessions and review enrolled authenticators, backup codes, and cloud sharing for unauthorized changes.
Review sign-in, identity administration and bulk file-access logs across connected services.

items.t: Andorra’s Social Security Fund confirms unauthorized access to identity records
items.x: data breach · social security · AD · Stolen employer digital certificates were used to access the declarants’ portal.

rec.title: Andorra’s Social Security Fund confirms unauthorized access to identity records
rec.summary: Andorra’s Social Security Fund reported misuse of stolen digital certificates to access a portal used by employers. It later reported data associated with 477,238 administrative identification numbers, not a count of living people. The fund said it had found no access to health or benefits records.
rec.vector: Stolen employer digital certificates were used to access the declarants’ portal.

sources.label: El Periòdic reporting the CASS director’s briefing

updates.text: The CASS director said data associated with 477,238 administration identification numbers was accessed. The figure includes records for deceased people.
Diari d’Andorra reported the fund had started sending personalized email notices to affected members.

affected: Administrative identification records held by CASS; identifiers do not equal living individuals.
payloads: Unauthorized users used stolen certificates to retrieve identity details through a legitimate portal. CASS did not report direct access to its internal databases.
guidance: Verify messages through official CASS channels; do not share sign-in codes or financial details in response to unsolicited contact.
Administrators should revoke exposed certificates, reissue trusted credentials and alert on unusual access to identity records.

items.t: CSC Telecom corrected an exposure affecting a database of text messages
items.x: third-party breach · telecommunications · LV · Exposed database

rec.title: CSC Telecom corrected an exposure affecting a database of text messages
rec.summary: Cybernews reported that an exposed CSC Telecom database contained more than 125 million text messages, not 125 million people. CSC Telecom said it blocked access and found no evidence that customer data had been copied. The Latvian Data State Inspectorate opened an inquiry.

sources.label: Cybernews research on the exposed database
Latvian Public Broadcasting, quoting CSC Telecom

updates.text: CERT.lv told LETA it had asked CSC Telecom to investigate, had offered assistance, and had forwarded its information to law enforcement.
The data protection regulator requested further information on the possible exposure, the scale and categories of data, and CSC Telecom’s response.
TVNET reported that the Data State Inspectorate confirmed it had received a breach report and begun an inquiry.

affected: The reported messages were sent on behalf of organizations including Swedbank, SEB, and airBaltic; the number of people whose data may have been exposed is unknown.
payloads: A database holding years of text messages was accessible outside its intended scope. Unauthorized copying or misuse was not established.
guidance: Check account activity and treat unexpected requests for verification codes as suspicious.
Restrict direct database access, rotate access credentials and review exposure-window logs.

items.t: Chile investigates a cyber incident affecting its consular visa system

rec.title: Chile investigates a cyber incident affecting its consular visa system
rec.summary: Chile’s foreign ministry said it was conducting forensic analysis and the national cybersecurity agency confirmed it was investigating. The first report said the incident began in late October and affected the consular visa system. The initial access method and any data theft are unconfirmed.

sources.label: El Mostrador reporting the ministry and cyber agency responses
El Mostrador reporting naval intelligence involvement
DUPIN coverage of the Chilean consular-system incident

updates.text: El Mostrador reported that national naval intelligence personnel had offered support and that the incident had not yet been contained. The ministry did not respond to questions about that reported involvement.

affected: Chile Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular service and visa system
payloads: The cause of the incident and the scope of any data exposure remain unconfirmed.
guidance: Use the foreign ministry’s official channels to confirm visa-service availability. Preserve system and identity logs, isolate affected components and verify restoration before reconnecting them.

Osiris listed the campus on November 21; the listing did not independently establish the amount of exposed data.

affected: Kang Chiao International School’s Linkou campus administrative systems; police said other campuses were not known to be affected
payloads: Extortion emails were sent to some parents; the initial network access method was not disclosed.
guidance: Do not respond to extortion emails or open their links or attachments. Preserve the message and report it through a verified school channel.

rec.summary: Phala reported an intrusion affecting AI inference and some confidential virtual machine infrastructure. It identified the OpenRouter route for DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 and said some tenant credentials were misused.
affected: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 requests routed through Phala from October 21 to November 8; other models were not implicated by Phala’s audit.
payloads: Some request contents and application credentials had evidence of exposure.
guidance: Follow Phala’s incident guidance, rotate secrets present in affected requests or workloads, and review relevant service logs.

items.t: Fullerton Health confirms exposure of about 140,000 work pass holder records

rec.title: Fullerton Health confirms exposure of about 140,000 work pass holder records
rec.summary: Fullerton Health disclosed unauthorized access to a standalone server supporting Singapore’s Migrant Worker Primary Care Plan, detected on October 31. The company later said around 140,000 work pass holder records were compromised, including about 43,000 tied to expired passes. It said medical, health and personal financial data were not involved and access to care continued.

sources.label: The Straits Times, quoting Fullerton Health and the Ministry of Manpower
CNA on notification and impersonation risks

updates.text: Fullerton Health and the Ministry of Manpower said about 140,000 work pass records were affected. Fullerton Health said it isolated the server and planned a replacement.

affected: Work pass holders with records in the affected Primary Care Plan system.
payloads: Records may include names, foreign identification numbers, dates of birth and contact information. Fullerton Health said the data did not contain medical or personal financial information.
guidance: Verify employment and work permit messages with the employer or Ministry of Manpower independently. Check official FWMOMCare notices.
Preserve access logs, review exposure by record and rebuild the affected service in an isolated environment with least-privilege access.

Zurich Japan, for data previously entrusted to PCS

guidance: Revoke sessions and credentials for affected vendor systems and verify containment before reconnecting them.

items.t: Attacker sweeps Avalanche Safe wallet through stale token approval
items.x: crypto hack · cryptocurrency · multi · A contract was deployed at an unused Avalanche address that already had unlimited token approval from the Safe wallet.

rec.title: Attacker sweeps Avalanche Safe wallet through stale token approval
rec.summary: An attacker deployed a contract at an unused Avalanche address that already had unlimited permission to move tokens from a Safe multisig wallet, then used it to sweep the wallet. A front-running bot’s copied transaction was confirmed first and offered to return funds for a bounty; a Safe owner agreed on-chain that it could keep 42,500 WAVAX, worth about $371,000.
rec.vector: A contract was deployed at an unused Avalanche address that already had unlimited token approval from the Safe wallet.

rec.summary: German B2B retailer TAKKT disclosed on 21 October a cyberattack on IT systems of its Industrial & Packaging division in Europe and Foodservices division in North America, taking systems offline. On 20 November it said operations had largely been restored and cut its full-year forecast, now expecting organic sales of around -7% and free cash flow lower by €10–30 million.

updates.text: TAKKT lowered earnings expectations; order processing, deliveries and invoicing were largely restored, but delays pushed some payments into 2027.

rec.summary: Railway said an attacker partly escaped isolation in its multi-tenant build system and accessed internal systems, decrypting customer environment variables. rec.title: AfD confirms September theft of mailboxes hosted by a service provider
rec.summary: The party confirmed that mailboxes hosted by a service provider were stolen in September. Reporters reviewed an archive containing roughly 420,000 emails, not 420,000 people; the party said some published material could be forged.

sources.label: heise online on the party’s confirmation
t-online on the November reporting and authenticity checks

updates.text: New reporting discussed contents of the previously disclosed archive. Authentication of the material remained incomplete.

affected: Alternative for Germany (AfD) and its email hosting service.
payloads: Mailboxes were copied and material appeared publicly. The initial access mechanism and authenticity of all material were not established.
guidance: Reset affected accounts and invalidate active sessions. Review mailbox rules, admin audit trails and recovery methods.
Use verified channels for unexpected contact that references internal correspondence.

items.t: Cysic reports unauthorized minting on its cross-chain bridge

rec.title: Cysic reports unauthorized minting on its cross-chain bridge
rec.summary: Cysic reported about 10 million unauthorized CYS tokens minted on BNB Smart Chain in October. It said 7.2 million had been sold, 2.8 million were frozen and transfers resumed by October 28. It said the later token burn did not recover the attacker’s proceeds.

updates.text: Cysic said transfers had resumed by October 28 and emphasized that the remediation burn did not recover stolen proceeds.
The Defiant cited PeckShield tracking approximately $744,000 in related funds. This is a traced amount, not a project-confirmed loss total.

affected: Cysic cross-chain bridge on BNB Smart Chain
payloads: Unauthorized minting inflated the bridge token supply.
guidance: Use the official Cysic bridge and follow notices on transfer availability. Monitor cross-chain issuance against reserves and require independent authorization for exceptional minting.

items.t: Weak seed generation enables theft from Qubic wallets
items.x: crypto hack · cryptocurrency · multi · Wallet seeds generated with Math.random() were reportedly reconstructable using values exposed in unencrypted network tr…

rec.title: Weak seed generation enables theft from Qubic wallets
rec.summary: Qubic wallet secret seeds were generated using Math.random(), while other numbers from the same random sequence were exposed in unencrypted network traffic. SlowMist demonstrated that six such numbers could be enough to reconstruct a wallet seed, and Qubic reported that about 2.94 trillion QU was taken from 1,404 wallets.
rec.vector: Wallet seeds generated with Math.random() were reportedly reconstructable using values exposed in unencrypted network traffic.

items.t: CISA confirms exploitation of a REDCap vulnerability

rec.title: CISA confirms exploitation of a REDCap vulnerability
rec.summary: CISA listed CVE-2026-90817 as actively exploited on November 18. Rescana cites an October 7 Unit 42 report observing exploitation for cryptocurrency mining. The reviewed sources do not quantify affected deployments.

updates.text: CISA added the REDCap vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

affected: REDCap installations
payloads: Unit 42 observed cryptocurrency mining on compromised systems, according to Rescana.
guidance: Upgrade to 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS, 17.4.4 Standard, or a current supported version confirmed by REDCap.
Preserve evidence and investigate public-facing deployments for signs of compromise before assuming patching alone resolved the incident.

items.t: Denmark confirms unauthorized access to its Central Person Register
items.x: data breach · government · DK · Misuse of a company’s authorized access to the register

rec.title: Denmark confirms unauthorized access to its Central Person Register
rec.summary: Denmark’s Central Person Register said an unauthorized party misused a private company’s legitimate access and obtained names, addresses and identification numbers for approximately 8.8 million registered people. This figure includes people who live abroad or are deceased. The government disclosed the incident on October 5; November password coverage refers to that earlier breach.
rec.vector: Misuse of a company’s authorized access to the register
affected: Denmark’s Central Person Register; approximately 8.8 million registered people, including deceased people and people living abroad.
payloads: An unauthorized party used a private company’s legitimate access to retrieve names, addresses and national identification numbers.
guidance: Verify unexpected correspondence with Danish authorities using independently obtained contact details. Organizations with access should monitor lookup volume and follow the CPR administrator’s update…

items.t: Gyazo breach affected 23.62 million account records and image metadata
items.x: data breach · image hosting · JP · Image upload server vulnerability

rec.title: Gyazo breach affected 23.62 million account records and image metadata
rec.summary: Helpfeel reported that an intrusion into Gyazo affected about 23.62 million account records, not that many unique people, and hundreds of millions of image metadata records. Forensics confirmed that 432 image files belonging to 133 users were viewed or obtained, but found no evidence of large-scale acquisition of image files. The logs did not identify exactly which records were transferred.

sources.label: Helpfeel’s final report and November 5 correction

updates.text: Helpfeel added about 174 million metadata records for deleted images to the disclosed scope; this did not mean those image files were taken.
Gyazo resumed service after security checks and other countermeasures.
Final forensics confirmed that 432 files belonging to 133 Gyazo users were viewed or obtained. Logs did not establish the exact contents of the outbound transfer.
Helpfeel corrected the scope of deleted-image metadata to about 1.12 million associated accounts. The 174 million figure counts metadata records, not accounts or image files.

affected: Gyazo account data, including about 5.62 million records linked to registered email addresses and about 18.01 million anonymous account records.
Separate image metadata sets included records for deleted images. Helpfeel did not find evidence that the corresponding deleted image files were acquired.
payloads: An intrusion through Gyazo’s image upload server led to database access. Investigators observed large database reads and an outbound transfer, but logs did not capture its contents.
Helpfeel reported exposure of password hashes, not plaintext passwords, and did not confirm exposure of payment information.
guidance: Reset your Gyazo password if you have not already done so. Change reused passwords on other services and review older images before restoring their sharing access.
For workplace accounts, review older screenshots for credentials or other secrets. Revoke exposed secrets and review sign-in and integration activity.

rec.title: CSDD confirms theft of payment-receipt data relating to 1.2 million people
rec.summary: The Road Traffic Safety Directorate reported on August 18 that an attacker had obtained its payment-receipt data relating to 1.2 million people. The receipt data dates back to 2008. CSDD said customer telephone numbers and email addresses were not compromised.

sources.label: Latvian Public Broadcasting on CSDD’s first disclosure
Latvian Public Broadcasting, chronology of disclosures

updates.text: CSDD quantified the breach at 1.2 million people and described the receipt data affected.

affected: People with payment receipts held by Latvia’s Road Traffic Safety Directorate.
payloads: The affected receipt data included identity details, payment amounts and dates, vehicle registration numbers, and some addresses.
guidance: Verify messages requesting payment through official CSDD channels.
Limit access to retained receipts, preserve access logs and monitor for bulk exports.

rec.title: South Korea fines KT $39 million over customer data breach
rec.summary: South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission fined KT KRW 53.979 billion, reported as $39 million, over data-protection violations. The earlier breach compromised the provider for nearly 11 months, exposed data of more than 16,000 subscribers, and enabled more than $167,000 in fraudulent mobile payments.

updates.text: Coverage reported the South Korean privacy regulator’s KRW 53.979 billion fine against KT over the breach.

rec.summary: Tata Electronics disclosed a cybersecurity incident on June 22. Researchers told Reuters that World Leaks posted files purporting to contain Apple and Tesla component documents. Reuters reviewed material later reported to include iPhone supplier details but did not verify the files' authenticity.

sources.label: Reuters review of the reported supplier documents, via Dawn

updates.text: Tata Electronics said it had detected a cybersecurity incident.
Reuters reported reviewing files purporting to identify components, suppliers and test photographs for unreleased iPhones. It did not verify the material's authenticity.

affected: Tata Electronics confirmed an incident. Apple and Tesla are the customers named in Reuters’ reporting on the purported files.
payloads: A ransomware group claimed to have taken and published supplier documents. Reuters reviewed some files but did not verify their authenticity; Tata did not disclose an initial access method.
guidance: Review supplier access to design repositories and logs for unusual exports. Revoke unnecessary sharing permissions and coordinate containment and verification with affected partners.
